terms.gloss: don’t go off anywhere too far
terms.grammar: nē with the present subjunctive of abeō; quō “anywhere”; longius “too far”
evidence: Plaut. Men. 327: proin tū nē quō abeās longius ab aedibus
Ter. Haut. 212: vidē sīs nē quō hinc abeās longius
terms.comment: Plautus and Terence both say it so, Terence with vidē sīs, “mind, please”. For a child who runs on ahead, nōlī praecurrere (see ahead).

phrases.english: Don’t run on ahead; walk with me.

phrases.latin: proin tū nē quō abeās longius ab aedibus
phrases.english: so don’t you go off anywhere far from the house

phrases.latin: Tū, ut tempus est diēī, vidē sīs nē quō hinc abeās longius.
phrases.english: You, seeing the time of day, mind you don’t go off anywhere far from here.

sources: Lewis & Short: abeo · Lewis & Short: longe
